prompt_en:
Create a vertical photorealistic fine-art fashion photograph on a luminous blue shoreline at low tide. One unmistakably adult woman in her mid-twenties walks ankle-deep through the water while steadying the brim of her straw hat. She wears an airy ankle-length white linen sundress and a natural woven straw hat. Her present face carries a small warm smile, with convincing near-human realism in her face, skin, hands, and posture.

The photographed world has an ordinary physical baseline of coherent sea, sand, sunlight, and anatomy, yet one temporal phase rule fails across secondary traces: every secondary trace lags exactly one second behind her present body. Her wet-sand reflection preserves the neutral face from just before her smile; the reflection answers with a different affect, the same face with one affect difference. Her shadow keeps the lowered hand from before she touched the hat. The foam ring around her ankles outlines the foot placement from one step earlier. The same temporal lag repeats across materials: wet-sand reflection, cast shadow, and ankle foam. All three traces share the same precise delay.

Use three-quarter full-body vertical framing that keeps her face, hat, wet-sand reflection, cast shadow, and ankle foam within one coherent view. Low natural sunlight creates a readable long shadow while retaining luminous blue water, warm straw texture, and delicate white fabric detail. The unaffected scene remains coherent in anatomy, perspective, lighting, fabric, and water; all other realism cues stay coherent. Optically clean photographic capture preserves natural lens and sensor response. The lens, exposure, color, and fine grain remain optically clean and natural, so the anomaly belongs entirely to the photographed world. At first glance the image is serene coastal beauty; on inspection, the localized reflection-timing mismatch creates a quiet second-look contradiction and quiet almost-right discomfort.
